# Overview {#sec-overview}

H9c2 rat cardiomyoblasts are used here as a **proxy for right-ventricular heart
failure**: phenylephrine (**PHE**) drives a hypertrophic / stress remodelling of
the proteome, and **mitochondrial transplantation** (Mito) is tested as a rescue.
The design is a clean **2 × 2 factorial** — PHE stress crossed with Mito
transplant — with **6 replicates per group**:

| `group` | PHE stress | Mito transplant | Role | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Ctl`      | – | – | Negative control (untreated) | 6 |
| `Mito`     | – | + | Transplant-only control | 6 |
| `PHE`      | + | – | Positive control (phenylephrine disease model) | 6 |
| `PHE_Mito` | + | + | Disease + mitochondrial-transplant rescue | 6 |

The factorial yields five contrasts, each answering one mechanistic question:

| Contrast | Definition | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **`CTLvPHE`** | `PHE − Ctl` | **Disease** — PHE stress remodelling |
| **`CTLvMITO`** | `Mito − Ctl` | **Intervention** — transplant alone |
| **`PHEvPHE_MITO`** | `PHE_Mito − PHE` | **Rescue** — transplant under stress |
| **`Interaction`** | `(PHE_Mito − PHE) − (Mito − Ctl)` | **Interaction** — PHE-dependence of transplant |
| **`MITOvPHE_MITO`** | `PHE_Mito − Mito` | Secondary |

We model **simple effects + the interaction** (not bare main effects), because
the biological question is whether transplant *rescues the stressed proteome*.

Architecture mirrors the shared house style: numbered self-cleaning stages, each
with `a_script/` (code), `b_reports/` (proteoDA QC PDFs), `c_data/` (RDS
hand-off + one consolidated `.xlsx`).

```
00_input/        raw matrix, metadata, contaminant references, R/ helpers
01_Filtering/    keratin + FBS-serum + missingness + outlier filtering
02_Normalization/ cycloess + (imp4p | mscoreutils) imputation
03_DEP/
  a_non_imputed/  PRIMARY limma DE (NA-tolerant)
  b_imputed/      imputed DE (concordance check)
04_Figures/       consolidated publication composites (F01–F06)
```

# Stage 00 — Inputs {#sec-inputs}

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `00_input/H9c2_raw.xlsx` | DIA-NN protein matrix, **5,002 protein groups** × (6 annotation + 24 samples) |
| `00_input/H9c2_meta.csv` | Metadata (`Col_ID`, `Group`, `Replicate`, …); `Replicate` is a **real block** |
| `00_input/hao_cellculture_contaminants.fasta` | Frankenfield 2022 Hao cell-culture contaminant FASTA (bovine = FBS serum) |
| `00_input/hpa_secreted_to_blood.txt` | HPA "Secreted to blood" gene list (419 genes) |

Groups, the design formula, the five contrasts, thresholds, and the contaminant
classifier are written **inline** in the 00–03 stage scripts (no shared config or
helper modules) — each script reads top-to-bottom as the actual workflow.

**`Replicate` is a genuine experimental block** (paired plate / day / passage
across all four groups, user-confirmed). It is modelled as a random block in DE
(§4) — not a nuisance to ignore.

# Stage 01 — Filtering {#sec-filtering}

## Contaminant removal: keratin + FBS serum {#sec-contaminants}

Cell-culture proteomes carry two contaminant classes that are *not* H9c2
biology:

1. **Keratins** — skin/hair handling contamination, removed by regex
   (`^Krt[0-9]|^Krtap` on gene symbol, `^Keratin` on description).
2. **FBS serum** — fetal bovine serum proteins from the culture medium. Rather
   than a hand-typed list, the serum panel is **reference-derived**: the
   intersection of the **bovine** Hao cell-culture contaminant FASTA with HPA
   **"Secreted to blood"** genes. Requiring *both* (bovine origin **and**
   plasma-secreted) avoids deleting abundant *cellular* bovine proteins that map
   to real H9c2 orthologues (actin, GAPDH, myoglobin) — the same keep-real-biology
   logic the CvH blood filter uses.

```{r}
#| label: contaminant-filter
# FBS serum panel = bovine Hao FASTA entries intersected with HPA "Secreted to blood"
hao_hdr  <- grep("^>", readLines(here::here("00_input", "hao_cellculture_contaminants.fasta"), warn = FALSE), value = TRUE)
bovine   <- toupper(na.omit(stringr::str_match(hao_hdr, "GN=([^ ]+)")[, 2][
              grepl("Bos taurus", stringr::str_match(hao_hdr, "OS=(.*?) OX=")[, 2])]))
secreted <- toupper(readLines(here::here("00_input", "hpa_secreted_to_blood.txt"), warn = FALSE))
serum    <- sort(intersect(unique(bovine), secreted))

is_keratin <- grepl("^Krt[0-9]|^Krtap", annotation$gene, ignore.case = TRUE) |
              grepl("^Keratin", annotation$description, ignore.case = TRUE)
is_serum   <- toupper(annotation$gene) %in% serum & !is_keratin
annotation <- annotation[!(is_keratin | is_serum), ]   # keratin + FBS serum removed
```

## Missingness + outliers {#sec-missing-outliers}

Native `filter_proteins_by_group` keeps proteins with ≥4 valid values in ≥1
group; the same 4-method outlier consensus as CvH (missingness, median-MAD, PCA
Mahalanobis, correlation; drop at ≥3/4) is applied.

```{r}
#| label: missingness
dal <- filter_proteins_by_group(dal, min_reps = 4, min_groups = 1,
                                grouping_column = "group")
```

**Frozen filtering log:**

| Step | Proteins after | Removed | % of raw |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw input | 5,002 | — | 100.0 |
| Contaminant removal (keratin + FBS serum) | 4,972 | 30 | 99.4 |
| Missingness (≥4 in ≥1 group) | **4,806** | 166 | 96.1 |

**No samples were flagged as outliers** — the final matrix is **4,806 proteins ×
24 samples** (balanced 6 per group), saved as
`01_Filtering/c_data/DAList_filtered.rds` with a consolidated
`filtering_report.xlsx`.

# Stage 02 — Normalization & imputation {#sec-norm}

Identical machinery to CvH: cyclic-loess via `normalize_data()`, bracketed by
`write_norm_report` / `write_qc_report`, then two **independent** imputation
options used only by complete-matrix methods (never the DE test):

```{r}
#| label: normalize
dal <- normalize_data(dal, norm_method = "cycloess")
saveRDS(dal, file.path(data_dir, "DAList_normalized.rds"))
# imputation/a_script/a_imp4p.R       -> imputation/c_data/DAList_imputed_imp4p.rds      (canonical, MCAR=mle / MNAR=igcda)
# imputation/a_script/b_mscoreutils.R -> imputation/c_data/DAList_imputed_mscoreutils.rds (mixed knn / QRILC)
```

# Stage 03 — Differential expression {#sec-dep}

## Model & the Replicate block {#sec-dep-model}

```{r}
#| label: dep-model
dal <- add_design(dal, "~ 0 + group + (1 | Replicate)")
dal <- add_contrasts(dal, contrasts_vector = c(
  "CTLvPHE       = PHE - Ctl",                        # Disease
  "CTLvMITO      = Mito - Ctl",                        # Intervention
  "PHEvPHE_MITO  = PHE_Mito - PHE",                    # Rescue
  "Interaction   = (PHE_Mito - PHE) - (Mito - Ctl)",  # Interaction
  "MITOvPHE_MITO = PHE_Mito - Mito"))                  # Secondary
dal <- fit_limma_model(dal)
dal <- extract_DA_results(dal, pval_thresh = 0.10, lfc_thresh = 0, adj_method = "BH")
```

`(1 | Replicate)` is routed through `limma::duplicateCorrelation`, giving one
consensus correlation (ρ̂ ≈ 0.02 — replicates are well-balanced, so the block
adds little here but is *correct* to include). The primary DE runs on the
**non-imputed** matrix (limma handles NAs); `b_imputed/` repeats it on the imp4p
and mscoreutils matrices as a concordance check. Significance via Π-score
(Xiao 2014, `Π = P.Value^|logFC|` < 0.05) and BH-FDR < 0.10.

## Frozen results {#sec-dep-results}

| Contrast | Role | FDR < 0.10 | Π < 0.05 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CTLvPHE` | Disease | 10 | 25 |
| `CTLvMITO` | Intervention | 135 | 67 |
| **`PHEvPHE_MITO`** | **Rescue** | **300** | 79 |
| `Interaction` | Interaction | 0 | 39 |
| `MITOvPHE_MITO` | Secondary | 0 | 28 |

The headline: the **Rescue** contrast (`PHE_Mito − PHE`) is the strongest signal
(300 FDR hits) — mitochondrial transplantation substantially remodels the
proteome of PHE-stressed cells. Transplant-alone (`CTLvMITO`, 135 hits) also
perturbs the proteome, while the formal `Interaction` has no FDR hits (the
rescue and intervention effects are largely additive at the per-protein level).

## Imputed concordance {#sec-dep-concordance}

Mito has far less missingness than CvH, so both imputation methods track the
non-imputed primary very closely (Spearman ρ on logFC):

| Method | range across 5 contrasts |
|---|---|
| **imp4p** (canonical) | ρ = 0.95 – 0.97 |
| mscoreutils | ρ = 0.95 – 0.96 |

This high concordance (vs CvH, where the weak contrast diverged) confirms the
Mito results are robust to imputation choice; the non-imputed primary remains
the reported DE.

# Reproducibility {#sec-repro}

```bash
Rscript 01_Filtering/a_script/01_run_filtering.R
Rscript 02_Normalization/a_script/01_run_normalization.R
Rscript 02_Normalization/imputation/a_script/a_imp4p.R          # canonical
Rscript 02_Normalization/imputation/a_script/b_mscoreutils.R    # comparison
Rscript 03_DEP/a_non_imputed/a_script/01_run_dep.R              # PRIMARY
Rscript 03_DEP/b_imputed/a_script/01_run_dep_imputed.R          # concordance
# then re-run the 04_Figures/ composites against 03_DEP outputs
```

**Key design decisions, in one place:**

- 2 × 2 factorial (PHE × Mito), 6 replicates/group; report simple effects + interaction.
- `Replicate` modelled as a real random block via duplicateCorrelation.
- Contaminant removal = keratin regex + bovine-FBS ∩ HPA-secreted serum panel
  (reference-derived, keeps real cellular biology).
- DE test on the **non-imputed** matrix; imputation (imp4p canonical) only for
  complete-matrix methods (figures, WGCNA).
- Π-score (Xiao 2014) for significance + effect size; BH-FDR < 0.10.
- Rescue contrast (`PHE_Mito − PHE`) is the primary biological readout.
